sentences.text: Henodus was a creature approximately one meter in length and one meter wide, possessing a flattened shell that resembled a modern turtle due to convergent evolution.
Its armor consisted of a plastron on the underside and a carapace on top, where the carapace extended beyond the limbs and was made of many bone pieces forming a mosaic pattern.
The shell was fused to the spine with normally positioned limbs, short legs featuring webbed toes, and a short, flat tail that moved side-to-side.
Weak limbs suggest it spent little time on land, and unlike modern turtles, it could not retract its head under its shell.
Henodus is the only known placodont found in non-marine deposits, suggesting it inhabited brackish or freshwater lagoons.
It possessed baleen-like denticles and used a toothless horny beak to pull up prey before crushing hard shells with its molars.
Fossils of Henodus chelyops have been found in Germany and Portugal, and the genus was described by Huene in 1936 within the family Henodontidae.
Henodus swam to the sea floor near the coast to find food, with a preferred diet including clams, chitons, limpets, and oysters.
Wide and very strong jaws, powered by powerful muscles and supported by the palatal and lower jaw bones, provided great biting force to crush shells.
The animal likely used its legs like flippers to improve swimming performance.
Henodus lived during the Late Triassic period, specifically the early Carnian age, between 237 and 227.3 million years ago.
